notes.title: Can now view random generated seeds as well as set a custom seed.
notes.content:
You can now enter a custom seed when picking a difficulty mode or leave it empty to just use a randomly generated seed. 

You can also view seeds by going to the pause menu to record or share the seed for others to try too. 
The seed will also show on death or escape. 

For those who don't know seeds let the randomness of the game be re-generated exactly as according to the seed value. 

The only thing that is not re-generated with the same seed value are what non-puzzle notes get spawned and where. 

Regards,
George

notes.title: Update 1.031
notes.content:
The previous flashlight note before this patch was partially descriptive in one paragraph and a bit confusing/misleading in the second paragraph it seems. 

In attempt to make the note more helpful and less confusing the second paragraph has been reworded with this small patch.

notes.title: Update 1.03
notes.content:
Improved Note Reading.
Changed Priest Font. 
Added the ability to print note text as you read it. 
Added text indication to indicate how to back out when reading note. 
Player HUD now hidden when reading note. 
You can still rotate note by moving mouse while holding left click or right click.

notes.title: Patch 1.01 Quality of Life Changes
notes.content:
In patch 1.01 I've done some subtle quality of life changes. 

Desks that can't be interacted with will now be indicated as such. 
Props will now also indicate what key should be pressed when hovering over them. 

I've also introduce a beta branch you can opt into via the game's properties in Steam. 
This beta branch updates the game to Unreal Engine 4.23 and may help with crashes some folks are experiencing. Please leave feedback if the beta branch is more stable for you.

Thanks for playing!

George Erfesoglou

notes.title: Excited to be releasing September 10th!
notes.content:
[b]RELEASE IMMINENT![/b]

As a fan of horror games of all kinds, I wanted to create a game that would keep the player tense and on edge in a unpredictable, novel and challenging way. 

This urge led to the conception of Two Till Midnight back in 2017, where I started playing with some novel mechanics using a protagonist who was nearsighted and requires glasses to see well. 

While some horror games have protagonists that wear glasses none I know ever use those glasses as an actual game mechanic. With Two Till Midnight I include glasses as part of the horror experience along with a compelling story, random elements and no saves.

I'm very happy to finally see my project go from an idea in my head to an experience I feel is ready to be shared with others. I personally have racked up many terrifying hours playing my own game and I hope you will too!

Thanks and have fun,

George
